Adjacent triangles share one side; triangle 3 partially overlaps with the gray triangle 0, but does not completely cover it. The problem states that the largest angle of each isosceles triangle is 100°, and in the figure this largest angle corresponds to the angle formed by the two sides at the common central vertex. Therefore, from triangle n to triangle n+1, it is equivalent to rotating 100° around the common center point. For triangle n to completely cover triangle 0, the accumulated rotation angle 100n needs to be an integer multiple of 360°, that is, 100n ≡ 0 (mod 360). Dividing both sides by 20 gives 5n ≡ 0 (mod 18). Since 5 and 18 are coprime, the smallest positive integer n is 18.

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: the grey triangle 0 and triangles 1, 2, 3 all have one vertex at the same central point, and each next triangle shares one of the two equal sides of the previous triangle, forming a spiral. From the text, each triangle is isosceles and its largest angle is 100°. In the picture, the largest angle is the central angle between the two shared radial edges. Therefore moving from triangle n to triangle n+1 rotates the whole triangle by 100° about the common central vertex. Triangle n exactly covers triangle 0 when the accumulated rotation is a whole number of full turns: 100n is divisible by 360. Solve the modular condition 100n ≡ 0 mod 360. Dividing by 20 gives 5n ≡ 0 mod 18. Since 5 and 18 are coprime, the smallest positive n is 18.
